memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "He was not among Korah's followers, who banded together against the LORD, but he died for his own sin and left no sons. Why should our father's name disappear from his clan because he had no son? Give us property among our father's relatives." - Num 27:3b-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The sisters continue their appeal with care and honesty. They make clear that their father was not part of Korah's rebellion against the Lord; he died for his own ordinary sin, as all people do. Then they ask a heartfelt question: why should their father's name disappear simply because he had no son? They long for their father's memory and portion to continue.

Notice what lies beneath their request. These women believed that God would give Israel the land. The inheritance they asked for did not yet exist in their hands; the nation had not even entered Canaan. Their appeal was an act of faith in God's promise. They were confident enough in God's word to plan for an inheritance still in the future.

Their concern for their father's name reveals hearts that valued family, legacy, and belonging within God's people. They did not want to be cut off from the community's inheritance. This was not mere self-interest but a desire to remain part of what God was giving to His people.

Faith like this takes God's promises seriously enough to act on them. Because the sisters trusted that God would keep His word, they made their request boldly. In Christ, we too are heirs of promises not yet fully seen, and we live by faith in the God who cannot fail (Heb 11:1). Let their confident faith stir yours to trust God's sure word.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you take God's promises seriously enough to act on them?
2. How does faith in God's future promises shape your decisions today?
3. What does it mean to live as an heir of God's promises in Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me faith that takes Your promises seriously and acts on them boldly. Help me live as a confident heir of all You have promised in Christ, trusting Your word that never fails. Amen.
